notes: This contract records the bounded IEEE 1516.1-2025 resign-action transition now implemented in Umbra's opt-in, non-installable development profile. Directive 1 makes the resigning federate's owned attributes unowned and emits current eligible Request Attribute Ownership Assumption callbacks; directive 2 deletes objects for which it owns HLAprivilegeToDeleteObject and emits Remove Object Instance callbacks; standalone directive 3 cancels the resigning federate's pending acquisition work before a voluntary resignation completes, including a regular request, a selected negotiated-divestiture confirmation with its stale owner callbacks, and an If Available reservation with its stale requester callback; the direct voluntary directive-4 regression deletes a delete-privileged object before divesting the retained object's remaining attribute; and directive 5 applies the same cancellation before combined delete/divest cleanup. The final-federate rule in 4.12.4 is also covered: directive 2 is applied even when the final federate supplies NO_ACTION. The public resignation path now also reserves a selected service-report-file serial inside its final membership transaction, after all ordinary rejection paths and before removal of the joined member, then appends the one type-44 HLAresignAction record before releasing the writer. The bounded Connection Lost slice proves that configured DELETE_OBJECTS, UNCONDITIONALLY_DIVEST_ATTRIBUTES, DELETE_OBJECTS_THEN_DIVEST, CANCEL_PENDING_OWNERSHIP_ACQUISITIONS, and CANCEL_THEN_DELETE_THEN_DIVEST Automatic Resign Directives reach their corresponding deletion/removal, divestiture/assumption, combined ordering, and stale-acquisition cleanup paths. The bounded continuation search now reconsiders an unowned attribute after a later eligible publication or join/discovery transition, while suppressing duplicate offers. A directed-interaction companion now proves that voluntary NO_ACTION resignation does not discard an already accepted timestamped directed payload when its target remains owned by another federate; an independent regulator releases the survivor before its grant and the callback retains the target, departed producer, timestamp/order, tag, and retraction metadata. A matching object-deletion companion retains an accepted timestamped Remove Object Instance payload and drains two recipient-local ledgers after the producing owner resigns with UNCONDITIONALLY_DIVEST_ATTRIBUTES. Resignation now preflights every eligible assumption recipient route before any delete/divest mutation, preserving the full federation state when an embedded callback route is unavailable. The tests also retain the official FederateOwnsAttributes and OwnershipAcquisitionPending rejection boundaries. This is source/test traceability only, not a service catalog entry, JUnit result, protected-review result, package claim, or conformance claim. Complete owner-search/arbitration after terminal callbacks, the bounded NO_ACTION forced-resign policy, full forced-resign disposition policy, remote transport, and remaining ownership forms remain separate work.

The target remains owned by a surviving federate, the source leaves with NO_ACTION, and the recipient's independent regulator releases one callback before its grant. The private retraction ledger records voluntary producer departure separately from the connection-loss cutoff marker; this is not a complete resignation-action or conformance matrix.
